summary: Charles A. Moore was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. at Yale University. He taught at Yale and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1936 to 1967, also founding Philosophy East and West.
Charles Alfred Bell worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Winchester College from circa 1884 to 1889 and at New College from circa 1889 to 1891.

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who earned his PhD in History of Religions under Paul Groner at the University of Virginia. He served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America.
Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a position at the University of Geneva from circa 1893 to 1939.

Charles Burnett is a historian, philosopher, and Indologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held posts at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and the Warburg Institute, where he became a professor in 1999.

Charles Cutler Torrey worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary from 1892 to 1900 and served as a professor at Yale University from 1900 to 1932.

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro.
Charles DiSimone is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at the University of Munich and Ghent University, where he is a permanent member and co-director.

Charles Duroiselle was a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as professor of Pali at the University of Rangoon and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma from 1912 to 1940.

Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned multiple degrees from the University of London. He taught at SOAS, served as Commissioner of Archaeology for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956–1967), and presided over the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

Charles Eliot worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology after studying at Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Foreign Office, as principal of the University of Hong Kong (circa 1912–1918), and at the University of Sheffield.
Charles Elliott was an Indologist and historian who worked for the East India Company and served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1837 to 1856.
Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School. From 1913 to 1934, he held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and the University of London.
Charles Goodman is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard. He has served as an Associate Professor at Binghamton University.
Charles H. Long was a scholar of religious studies who earned his BD and PhD at the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara.

Charles Hallisey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Colgate, Harvard Divinity School, Penn, and the University of Chicago. He has held faculty positions at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served at Presidency University from 1866 to 1892, including as head, and later worked as Librarian of the India Office Library from 1892 to 1903.

Charles Li is a scholar working in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He has held posts as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of British Columbia and as a project researcher at the University of Hamburg.

Charles Malamoud is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held positions at the University of Lyon and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1979 to 1998.
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist who studied at New College from circa 1878 to 1882. He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1883 to 1946.
